issues.title: Ill-defined normal-trace graph space
issues.failure_explanation: Before DefH1Gamma, the old source constructs γ1 only as a map from H1(ω,Δ) to H^{-1/2}(Γ). DefH1Gamma nevertheless applies γ1 to arbitrary members of H1(ω), so its membership condition uses an operator outside its stated domain. Its subsequent norm is also not defined on the stated set, because membership of γ1v in H^{-1/2}(Γ) does not imply that the L2(Γ) norm appearing there is finite. Thus the claimed normal-trace space and its Hilbert-space structure are not well defined.
issues.overall_effect: The functional-analytic domain used by the Friedrichs theorem is undefined as stated, and the theorem's compactness setting and the corollary's use of its normal trace lack a valid graph-space interface.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace DefH1Gamma by the completion, equivalently the closed graph, of H¹(ω,Δ) in H¹(ω)×H⁻¹ᐟ²(Γ), with graph norm formed from the H¹ norm and the H⁻¹ᐟ² normal-trace norm, and extend γ₁ continuously to that completion. Use H⁻¹ᐟ² consistently in the theorem and record the standard cutoff-and-density observation placing the locally Helmholtz-harmonic functions of CorTrace in this graph space.
issues.why_classification: This is a genuine definitional defect rather than a typo, since the old operator is used outside its domain and the stated norm is not defined. A standard local graph-completion correction supplies the intended Hilbert space and trace interface, while preserving the hypotheses, conclusions, constants, and scope of the Friedrichs theorem and CorTrace. It requires only routine functional-analytic checking and no substantive new lemma or loss.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: We define the Hilbert space $H^{1}\left(  \omega,\Gamma\right)$ as the completion of $H^{1}\left(  \omega,\Delta\right)  $

issues.title: Unsupported operator-norm continuity of the DtN family

failure_location.quote: depends continuously on the wavenumber $s\in\CutC$ and admits a continuous extension to $\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}$

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem's unqualified continuity assertion claims continuity of DtN(s) in the standard operator-norm topology. The old argument uses eqn:DtN_gh and dominated convergence for each fixed g and h, which yields continuity of each scalar pairing. Its dominating series depends on those fixed inputs and supplies no uniform estimate over their unit balls, so it does not establish operator-norm continuity or the operator-norm limit at zero. The revision instead states strong continuity and proves convergence in H^{-1/2} for every fixed input.
issues.overall_effect: The continuity and zero-wavenumber extension portions of thm:DtN are established only in a weaker topology by the old proof; its symmetry, boundedness, and sign estimates are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the operator-norm continuity and operator-norm limit by strong-operator continuity: for every fixed g∈H¹ᐟ²(S_R), require DtN(s)g to converge in H⁻¹ᐟ²(S_R), including convergence to DtN(0) as s→0. Prove this with the weighted Fourier-series estimate and dominated convergence, leaving the symmetry, boundedness, and sign estimates unchanged.
issues.why_classification: Strong continuity is a genuine weakening of uniform convergence on the input unit ball, so this is not a same-guarantee minor clarification. The surviving statement retains the same operator family, parameter domain, and zero-wavenumber limit for every fixed input, and its proof is a contained multiplier argument rather than a global reconstruction. The loss is therefore limited and the issue is moderate.

issues.title: Invalid varying-wavenumber compactness proof of the Friedrichs inequality

failure_location.quote:
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem is uniform over functions for which there exists a possibly different wavenumber s. Its negation therefore yields pairs (v_k,s_k) and convergence of the normal traces only in H^{-1/2}(S_R). The old proof instead calls the union over all parameters a Hilbert space, although continuity of each DtN(s) neither makes that union linear nor weakly closed, and it replaces the required H^{-1/2} convergence by L2 convergence. Consequently, passing the boundary condition to a weak limit with one fixed parameter is unjustified.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish the wavenumber-uniform Friedrichs inequality, and therefore does not establish the parts of CorTrace that invoke that inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the contradiction sequence as pairs (v_k,s_k), extract a subsequence weakly in H¹(Ω) and strongly in L²(Ω), and avoid treating the union of boundary-condition spaces as a Hilbert space. Apply the existing uniform real-part bound for DtN directly at each s_k: the positive multiple of ‖v_k‖²_{L²(S_R)} is bounded by |⟨∂_r v_k,overline{v_k}⟩|, which tends to zero because ∂_r v_k→0 in H⁻¹ᐟ² and the Dirichlet traces are bounded in H¹ᐟ². The weak trace limit of the resulting zero boundary traces is the trace of the constant L²-limit, forcing that constant to vanish and giving the required contradiction. CorTrace then continues to use the theorem unchanged.
issues.why_classification: The old compactness inference is genuinely invalid, so this is not a typo. However, the already-proved wavenumber-uniform coercive sign estimate supplies a short, routine local bypass that neither selects a limiting wavenumber nor needs a new lemma. It restores the full Friedrichs inequality and its dependent corollary without weakening any guarantee, so the least adequate repair is minor.
